assumptions.statement: The default thermal load - 900 C gas at a 500 W/(m²·K) film coefficient on the firing end - is a demonstration fixture. Real values depend on the engine, the operating point and the duty cycle. The film coefficient in particular is the most uncertain input in this model and the computed temperatures scale strongly with it.

This is a steady-state solution: it represents a sustained operating condition, not a warm-up, a transient load change or any part of the engine cycle. Cyclic peak surface temperatures are higher than a steady-state average.
The 150 C default cylinder-head seat temperature is a demonstration fixture and is applied as a fixed temperature, which assumes the head is an ideal sink with no contact resistance at the seat.

The 450 C to 850 C operating window is the commonly cited self-cleaning to pre-ignition range for a spark plug firing end. It is entered here as a demonstration fixture, not as a specification from a plug or engine manufacturer. Confirm the window that applies to your application.

The shell, insulator and electrode are modelled as perfectly bonded, so no contact thermal resistance is included at their interfaces. Real assemblies have some resistance, which would raise the computed firing-end temperature.

Simplified three-part spark-plug thermal template: centre electrode, ceramic insulator and metal shell as concentric solids of revolution with perfectly conducting interfaces. The hex, terminal, ground electrode arm, internal resistor, seals, gasket, thread form and precious-metal tips are not modelled. Thread major diameter, reach, seat position and electrode gap are preserved interfaces and cannot be changed by the optimizer.

scope.scope_statement: Genuine 3D steady-state heat-conduction finite-element analysis of the electrode / insulator / shell assembly, with convective heat input from the combustion side, conduction into the cylinder-head seat, and convection to air at the terminal end. Each part carries its own thermal conductivity and the interfaces between them are treated as perfectly conducting.
not_in_scope: Combustion, flame propagation and cylinder pressure
Spark and ignition discharge, and all electrical behaviour
In-cylinder gas flow and charge motion
Transient engine-cycle thermal response (this is a steady-state solution)
Contact thermal resistance between the shell, insulator and electrode
Deposit build-up, electrode erosion and service life
Mechanical stress, thread strength and sealing performance
scope.geometry_capability_note: Simplified three-part spark-plug thermal template: centre electrode, ceramic insulator and metal shell as concentric solids of revolution with perfectly conducting interfaces. The hex, terminal, ground electrode arm, internal resistor, seals, gasket, thread form and precious-metal tips are not modelled. Thread major diameter, reach, seat position and electrode gap are preserved interfaces and cannot be changed by the optimizer.

solver.name: scikit-fem steady-state conduction (quadratic tetrahedra)
solver.method_statement: 3D steady-state Fourier heat-conduction finite-element analysis with 10-node tetrahedra and per-material subdomains, verified against the analytical 1D conduction benchmark. Interfaces between assembled parts are treated as perfectly conducting. It does not model combustion, ignition discharge, cylinder pressure or flow, or any transient engine-cycle behaviour.

benchmarks.name: cantilever_beam_linear_static
benchmarks.description: End-loaded cantilever 200 x 20 x 20 mm, E = 210 GPa, nu = 0.3, tip load 1000 N, clamped at x = 0.
benchmarks.reference_source: Euler-Bernoulli tip deflection PL^3/(3EI) with the Timoshenko shear correction PL/(kGA), k = 5/6; peak bending stress M c / I.

max_bending_stress.reference_basis: Beam bending stress M c / I at the clamped root

notes: Peak stress is compared at a 10 percent tolerance because the fully clamped face is a stress concentration that beam theory does not represent.
Mesh: 1082 nodes, 3612 tetrahedra, 19962 displacement degrees of freedom.

benchmarks.name: bar_1d_steady_state_conduction
benchmarks.description: Steady-state conduction through a 100 x 20 x 20 mm bar, k = 45.0 W/(m·K), 800.0 K at x = 0 and 400.0 K at x = L, remaining faces adiabatic.
benchmarks.reference_source: Analytical 1D conduction: linear profile T(x) = T_hot + (T_cold - T_hot) x / L, heat flow Q = k A (T_hot - T_cold) / L.

max_nodal_temperature_error.reference_basis: Exact linear profile; any non-zero value is discretization error

heat_flow_through_cold_face.reference_basis: Analytical Q = k A dT / L

notes: Mesh: 396 nodes, 1220 tetrahedra, 2351 temperature degrees of freedom.

solver_verification.note: These benchmarks compare the same solver code path used for the results in this report against closed-form solutions.

recommendation.statement: Candidate 3 is the best feasible generated design, but it does not beat the baseline on peak temperature gradient (82.28 K/mm to 92.37 K/mm). Every candidate that reached a lower value violated a constraint. The baseline remains the best feasible design in the space searched so far.

mesh_convergence.statement: Re-solving the recommended design on a refined mesh (1695 to 22600 nodes) left the feasibility verdict unchanged, but these metrics are NOT mesh-converged: max_temperature_gradient_k_per_m +32.4% (tolerance 10%). The largest change is max_temperature_gradient_k_per_m at 32.4%. Stiffness and mass comparisons between candidates remain usable; the absolute peak values should be taken from a verification-fidelity run, and any candidate whose margin against a stress limit is smaller than this error should be re-checked.

narrative.headline: 4 design(s) generated, 3 evaluated by the solver, 3 feasible under the configured constraints, 1 failed to evaluate.
paragraphs: The design space was searched with seeded Latin-hypercube design of experiments. Every candidate was built by the parametric CAD generator, meshed, and solved with the same solver configuration before being judged, so the comparison between them is like-for-like.

Candidate 3 is the best feasible generated design, but it does not beat the baseline on peak temperature gradient (82.28 K/mm to 92.37 K/mm). Every candidate that reached a lower value violated a constraint. The baseline remains the best feasible design in the space searched so far.

Recommended design against the baseline: mass 0.02661 to 0.02705 kg (+1.7%); peak temperature 731.3 to 751.2 C (+2.0%); minimum temperature 413.8 to 410.8 C (-0.4%); peak temperature gradient 82.28 to 92.37 K/mm (+12.3%); heat flow through the sink surfaces 92.83 to 93.08 W (+0.3%).
Candidates that produced no result: 1 at the parameter_validation stage. They carry no metrics and are excluded from ranking.
caveats: Mean solver time per candidate was 1.7 s; the whole study took 137 s.

Re-solving the recommended design on a refined mesh (1695 to 22600 nodes) left the feasibility verdict unchanged, but these metrics are NOT mesh-converged: max_temperature_gradient_k_per_m +32.4% (tolerance 10%). The largest change is max_temperature_gradient_k_per_m at 32.4%. Stiffness and mass comparisons between candidates remain usable; the absolute peak values should be taken from a verification-fidelity run, and any candidate whose margin against a stress limit is smaller than this error should be re-checked.

These are virtual-prototyping predictions under the model you configured. They narrow down which designs are worth building; they do not replace physical testing or any approval your process requires.

standing_limitations: This report contains virtual-prototyping predictions produced under the engineering model recorded below. It is not a regulatory certification, not an approval for road use, and not a substitute for physical validation.
A candidate marked 'feasible under configured model' satisfied the constraints listed in this report and nothing more.

Material properties are taken from the catalog snapshot recorded with each run. Where a record is tagged 'illustrative_handbook_value' it is not supplier-certified data and must be replaced before any engineering sign-off.
Candidates that failed geometry generation, meshing or the solver carry no metrics. They are listed with their failure stage and reason rather than omitted.

assurance.note: Every verdict below was produced by the deterministic assurance service from a measurement. A check recorded as 'not_run' produced no evidence and is not a pass.

rungs.evidence_required: Hand-checkable temperature drops, heat flow and a closed energy balance.

rungs.capability: Three-dimensional steady conduction through shell, insulator and electrodes, with per-material conductivity.
rungs.evidence_required: Material and interface provenance, boundary-condition provenance, a mesh study and a closed energy balance.
rungs.release_label: Simulation evaluated under a declared reduced thermal model.

rungs.evidence_required: A stated operating point, a crank-angle or heat-flux model, and justification for the cycle averaging.
rungs.gap: The firing-end boundary is a declared convective film condition, not a combustion-derived heat flux. No engine operating point is represented, so the absolute temperature level is model-specific.

rungs.evidence_required: Sensor location, type and calibration, stated engine conditions and an independent validation dataset.
rungs.release_label: Validated only for the tested operating points.
rungs.gap: No thermocouple data. The published combustion-coupled work needed heat-transfer-coefficient tuning against measurement to reach ±10%, which this model has not had.

rungs.capability: Electrode erosion, oxidation and interface degradation.
rungs.evidence_required: Specialist multiphysics coupling plus microscopy, wear or erosion comparison.
rungs.release_label: Degradation prediction validated only within the tested domain.
rungs.gap: Steady conduction cannot represent arc discharge, plasma energy transfer or material ablation. This is a different physics path, not a refinement of S1.

fidelity_ladder.method: Closed-form analytical estimators: beam and plate bending, a thermal resistance network.
fidelity_ladder.use: Live preview while a parameter is being edited; initial screening.
fidelity_ladder.gate: A known solution with its model scope documented, and a measured calibration note against the finite-element path.

fidelity_ladder.method: Coarse finite-element analysis on the screening mesh.
fidelity_ladder.use: Rank broad design variants and remove clearly poor candidates.
fidelity_ladder.gate: Numerical checks passed and correlation to the refined mesh recorded.

fidelity_ladder.method: Refined finite-element analysis on the verification mesh.
fidelity_ladder.gate: Mesh convergence shown and the analytical benchmark passed.

fidelity_ladder.method: Reduced-order model or surrogate trained on verified F2 results.
fidelity_ladder.use: Many-query sensitivity and optimisation; fast what-if.
fidelity_ladder.gate: Holdout field error, stability, uncertainty, out-of-distribution detection and a deterministic fallback to F2.

fidelity_ladder.use: Validate the model and the decision for an intended-use domain.
fidelity_ladder.gate: A test protocol, measurement uncertainty, repeatability and an independent holdout.

checks.title: Unit consistency
checks.description: Every quantity entering the solver converts to canonical SI.
checks.detail: 8 unit-carrying quantities converted to canonical SI (m, N, Pa, kg, K, W/(m·K)).

checks.title: Dimensional plausibility
checks.description: The solid's overall size falls inside the envelope for its component type.
checks.detail: Largest overall dimension 46.0 mm, inside the 10-200 mm envelope.

checks.title: Material property completeness
checks.description: Every assigned material carries the properties this analysis consumes.
checks.detail: 4 material assignment(s) carry every property this analysis consumes, each with a declared condition.

checks.title: Geometry integrity
checks.description: The solid is valid, watertight and has positive volume.
checks.detail: 3 valid solid(s), 4.0 cm3 total.

checks.title: Preserved interface invariance
checks.description: Protected interfaces measure what the specification requires.
checks.detail: 2 protected interface(s) held; largest deviation 0.00000 mm against an applied tolerance of 0.300 mm. This proves the interface to 0.300 mm, not to the 0.001 mm target: the measurement is taken on the tessellated solid, which cannot resolve finer. The deviation measured is well inside that, but only the applied tolerance is proven.

checks.title: Semantic region mapping
checks.description: Every boundary condition names a region the generator actually built.
checks.detail: 3 boundary condition(s) mapped to named semantic regions out of 5 available.

checks.title: Force-path declaration
checks.description: Pressure, piston force and reaction force are distinguished, not conflated.
checks.detail: No hydraulic force path applies to a spark_plug.

checks.title: Thermal boundary consistency
checks.description: A conduction model has both a heat input and a sink path, with consistent signs.
checks.detail: Heat flows from 'combustion_exposed_surfaces' at 1173 C to 'terminal_end_surfaces' at 353 C, a 820 K span across 3 boundary conditions.

checks.title: Mesh element quality
checks.description: No inverted or near-degenerate elements, measured by the gamma ratio.
checks.detail: Worst element gamma 0.138, mean 0.784 over 6663 elements; 0 below 0.1.

checks.title: Mesh volume fidelity
checks.description: The meshed volume matches the CAD volume.
checks.detail: Meshed volume 4.0 cm3 against a CAD volume of 4.0 cm3, a 0.715% difference (tolerance 2%).

checks.title: Result field integrity
checks.description: The stored result field is present, complete and finite.
checks.detail: 1031 nodes and 2058 surface triangles read back from result_fields_steady_state_operating.npz; every value finite across 3 stored arrays.

checks.title: Decision metric present
checks.description: The analysis produced the quantity the decision depends on.
checks.detail: max_temperature_k = 1004.44 (canonical SI), alongside 6 further computed metrics.

checks.title: Load and reaction balance
checks.description: Each assembled load integrates back to its intended resultant.
checks.detail: A steady-state conduction run applies no mechanical loads; its equivalent check is the energy balance.

checks.title: Boundary condition coverage
checks.description: Every boundary condition resolved to a non-zero mesh area.
checks.detail: 3 boundary condition(s) applied; smallest resolved area 313.1 mm2.

checks.title: Energy balance
checks.description: Every boundary is accounted for and the assembled system conserves energy. This is a consistency check, not an accuracy one.
checks.detail: power entering the solid across every boundary against power leaving it: 92.827 W in against 92.827 W out, a 0.0000% imbalance (tolerance 2%). A closed balance shows the model is self-consistent; it does not show the mesh is fine enough, which the convergence check covers separately.

checks.title: Linear solve residual
checks.description: The linear system converged to the required relative residual.
checks.detail: sparse direct factorisation (SuperLU) reached a relative residual of 5.717e-15 against an acceptance threshold of 1.0e-06.

provenance.label: The default thermal load - 900 C gas at a 500 W/(m²·K) film coefficient on the firing end - is a demonstration fixture. Real values depend on the engine, the operating point and the duty cycle. The film coefficient in particular is the most uncertain input in this model and the computed temperatures scale strongly with it.

This is a steady-state solution: it represents a sustained operating condition, not a warm-up, a transient load change or any part of the engine cycle. Cyclic peak surface temperatures are higher than a steady-state average.
The 150 C default cylinder-head seat temperature is a demonstration fixture and is applied as a fixed temperature, which assumes the head is an ideal sink with no contact resistance at the seat.

The 450 C to 850 C operating window is the commonly cited self-cleaning to pre-ignition range for a spark plug firing end. It is entered here as a demonstration fixture, not as a specification from a plug or engine manufacturer. Confirm the window that applies to your application.

The shell, insulator and electrode are modelled as perfectly bonded, so no contact thermal resistance is included at their interfaces. Real assemblies have some resistance, which would raise the computed firing-end temperature.

Simplified three-part spark-plug thermal template: centre electrode, ceramic insulator and metal shell as concentric solids of revolution with perfectly conducting interfaces. The hex, terminal, ground electrode arm, internal resistor, seals, gasket, thread form and precious-metal tips are not modelled. Thread major diameter, reach, seat position and electrode gap are preserved interfaces and cannot be changed by the optimizer.
